column8: Fri 20 Nov: 2.0 beside the definition of ink, the card's best: Tobin's 1958 risky asset was a default-free government bond, so the plan holds as safe what the founding separation paper held as risky, because her wealth is counted on ten Januaries; carries row 29's sentence (merged here); Tobin is 2.0's one outside name; said of the T-bonds and the Treasuries inside the funds, never of a fund's payout (IBTM pays net asset value).

Fri 20 Nov: 2.0 with row 1 as its second clause: shares were outside Tobin's paper on purpose (monetary assets only), so the plan sits nearer his original than the textbook's T-bills plus the market; one clause, never a second outside name.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into H3-020 (Tobin's two funds): adds Tobin's own words for separation, read at source, and that moving half of VT leaves its mix unchanged; H3-020 takes this as its source.

Fri 20 Nov: store or Q&A behind row 1: the theorem holds only while cash is riskless, and Tobin called cash only relatively riskless; H7-001 carries the date point (safe belongs to a date), row 5 the horizon.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.0 behind row 1, the hinge: Tobin himself wrote that the investor's year is not the same for all investors, so changing the year changes the safe asset; a footnote on costs, not a liability theory, so one clause at most.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e or Table 3, or one clause in 2.0: Tobin admitted no portfolio is irrevocably frozen, and IPS l.17 names the two reasons to change in advance and says a market fall is not one; reasons to change, never only two things can break the plan; beside Q57-040 (Sharpe's key), one outside name per part.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.0 or 2.3, one clause: Tobin proved no smooth taste for risk holds only the safe asset when the risky one pays more, so IPS l.11's none is a definition (CANON A4), not caution, and l.9 says her taste alone would usually own shares; in 2027 her whole first deposit sits in that excluded corner; never in 3f as why the first plan was dropped (l.9's reason, CANON A3); row 9 merged here.

Fri 20 Nov: Q&A behind row 7: a kinked investor insures completely with no deductible, and an all-or-nothing payment is that kink (Keel inference); the paper's word optimal stays inside its quote, never on the plan; working paper and Epstein read in excerpts.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q188-007: Skiadas states Tobin's result in textbook form and adds no use for Laura.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 or Q&A beside row 7: Sharpe and Tint's mean-variance rule put 34.8% of a fully funded dated promise (prepaid tuition) in shares, where IPS l.11 puts none; their illustration, not what Michigan or Wyoming held; their hedge was inflation-indexed, never offered for Laura (banned, and her payments are fixed dollars, TNA l.7).

Fri 20 Nov: store, the basis of rows 25-28: Sharpe and Tint's k from 0 to 1, with no setting between in Caplet's plan; the paper is a scan unread at source and three restatements agree, so read it before citing; row 28 merged here.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q188-013: a Keel derivation of the one-period form of Rudolf and Ziemba's verified result (the hedge does not depend on risk tolerance).

Fri 20 Nov: 2.2 or 2.3, the theorem behind the allocation is the rule: the liability hedge is independent of preferences, so the ten would be the same purchase for a bold or a timid Laura; their hedge is resized continuously, hers bought once and held; say the ten as the IPS does (T-bonds or iBond Treasury funds), with Q57-042 for the practice words; row 12 merged here.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.2 at most: 99.5% and 99.2% are Keel ratios not in NUMBERS, so a plan figure only if the numbers owner books them; otherwise say about equal to their cost, IPS l.13's roughly $300,000, with NUMBERS 1's $301,544 and the $2,388 top-up.

Fri 20 Nov: Q&A: Merton (1975) lets simple bonds serve as a fund, which answers the objection that ten Treasuries and a fund are not one safe asset; Q57-042 (Waring and Whitney's new two-fund theorem) carries the point more directly.

Fri 20 Nov: store: Merton's long-bond hedge done by date for the five T-bonds; falling rates still touch waiting interest (NUMBERS 2) and the iBond funds pay net asset value, never a fixed sum (NUMBERS 3), as the row says.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 or References: Merton's named exception, labour income that cannot be sold forward, is IPS l.9 in theory's words, so her career changes how much of the market she holds, not which; beside Q1c-028 and Q134-025, one outside name per part; row 31 merged here.
Fri 20 Nov: References or Q&A: Tobin himself named the covariance of returns with earnings from human capital in 1981, IPS l.9's argument; a second Tobin cite, so not in prose beside row 1.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 or 3e at most, and only reworded: as written it reads against IPS l.3 and l.9 (a career one cannot sell); an advance sells one contracted book's royalties forward in instalments, while new advances still come later and smaller in a slump; can, never does (Q95); Keel inference.
Fri 20 Nov: Q&A only: Buiter's two baskets is a second image, and nothing sits beside pencil and ink.
Fri 20 Nov: store: Tobin's reply to critics quoted only through Buiter; Tobin (1969a) unread.

Fri 20 Nov: store or Q&A for VT's case beside Q175: the CAPM fails at the first hurdle because few hold the market, and VT holds listed world shares, not every risky asset; never in 3f, which takes no outside names.

Fri 20 Nov: merged into H7-019 (no one can run on the ladder) and the reserve aha nobody can run on the plan: adds only that Tobin's investor never borrowed, by definition; Q2a-005 holds the forced gilt sales.
Fri 20 Nov: store: Tobin called allocation in stages permissible and perhaps indispensable; the order-of-purchase reserve aha already carries the plan's stages, which are promises, not asset classes.

Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q68-037 (the floor as a matching block bought before its promise), beside H7-067 (bought deal): adds Sharpe and Tint's order run backwards, a Keel synthesis with no source; the chiasmus is a slogan flip (D35 list), and the Treasuries bought in January 2028 and at the move are shares of the late-2032 Treasury fund, said so.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c, one clause: Leibowitz's 60/40 fund fell from full to 69% funded as rates raised its debts (Q1c-031), while her stated ends are counted after both are bought; name what is owned as shares of the late-2032 Treasury fund (blind judges, Thu 19 Nov), and keep NUMBERS 3's early-end case (up to $4,589 short at zero interest), so never cannot move.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.2 or 3b: tells a judge which numbers to argue with, but only two numbers overclaims, since the payments' zero-interest standard and the 0.5% margin are also choices about risk (NUMBERS 0, 2); say the IPS makes two such choices, most and half; 73.3% is Keel's reading of most with the $75,001 floor rule; half as the middle of NUMBERS 8o's trade, Caplet's choice, never optimal.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q188-011: the same no-setting-between point in the conceit's words; a stated end rests on shares of the late-2032 Treasury fund, said so (blind judges, Thu 19 Nov).
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q188-001: the sentence form of row 1 (same fear, opposite runs), with H7-001's date point; safe for a date is said of the Treasuries, never of a fund's payout.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q195-001 (card Q195 holds preferred habitat): Modigliani and Sutch's clienteles via Vayanos and Vila; the 1966 text unread.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q188-017: the career lies outside VT's market as Merton's exception says; Keel inference.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a or 2.3, the card's frame: an investor stays in the maturity that matches its debts unless paid to move; cite as McElhattan's 1975 summary, Modigliani and Sutch unread; Q188-030 merged here.
Fri 20 Nov: store or 3e: the habitat premium may be positive or negative, against Hicks's always-positive premium (H6-050); Q64-006 and Q64-007 hold the measured history.

Fri 20 Nov: a mapping row for 2.2: five of the ten are iBond Treasury fund shares that end on or about 15 December and pay net asset value (blind judges, Thu 19 Nov; NUMBERS 3), so never Treasuries ending 15 Dec 2032 without saying so.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a with row 23: habitat demand in the model is for zero-coupon bonds, and with STRIPS banned her coupons arrive before her dates, the extra Treasuries' reason; never offer zero-coupon Treasuries as Laura's option.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a with row 10: traders who carry rate risk earn the term premium, a risk she does not run holding to each date; the mechanism behind H3-015's slogan; a model, and Q64-034 says it works against her on the coupons.
Fri 20 Nov: store: pension funds hold long for duration, money-market funds short by mandate; her waiting cash sits with the second, which ETF still unverified (NUMBERS 0).
Fri 20 Nov: store: she takes the price others set (at most 0.022% of IBTM, NUMBERS 8w), which needs no calibration to say.

Fri 20 Nov: store until read at source: two mirrors of the ACM file differ by 0.06-0.08 points and the New York Fed file was unread, so no ACM figure is printed until checked; ACM stops at 10 years, so the 2038-2042 rungs have none.

Fri 20 Nov: store or 3e: the ACM history (charged in July 2020, paid in late 2026) comes from one conflicting mirror; read the New York Fed file and print a dated range with Kim-Wright (Q64-005, Q64-006), never one figure.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a or Table 3's note at most, the card's best: $19,000-$28,000 is Keel arithmetic on two model estimates by a parallel shift, not in NUMBERS, so the numbers owner books it before use; never roughly why the ten fit inside the first deposit (the yield level does that, and the premium is a model's split of it); the 0.62 comes from a conflicting mirror.

Fri 20 Nov: store: the build order's reason stays NUMBERS 1's (the longest rungs move most with yields); every affordable rung is bought on one day in January 2027, so the premium is no second reason; one mirror's figures.
Fri 20 Nov: a placement note: the premium belongs to 3a and 3c need not mention it; inference on one month of one mirror.
Fri 20 Nov: store or Q&A: why judges rarely know preferred habitat (a paragraph in MBA textbooks); supports niche for ideas 1-2.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a, one sentence: IPS l.11's rule does not depend on being paid, since UK pension funds bought long gilts at 0.48% above inflation; charged is an inference from an inverted index-linked curve, not a measured premium, and her bonds are nominal; check Greenwood and Vayanos line by line (fetch summary); row 16 merged here.
Fri 20 Nov: store: Britain answered its habitat with 50-year and long gilts; the US 2031-2036 gap is card Q93's, said as no Treasury bond.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q195-014: the scale of the same UK episode, read through a fetch summary.
Fri 20 Nov: store: the 2000 buybacks pushed the 20-year below the 5-year, the same surplus forecast that stopped the 30-year (card Q93); figures from a fetch summary, checked before print.

Fri 20 Nov: store: Denmark and the Netherlands are not in the abstract read, so drop them unless read; her rungs end by November 2041, so the 30-year minus 10-year spread speaks of the long end beyond her dates.
Fri 20 Nov: store: the Bank of England's map of gilt habitats; her 7.76 years would sit with insurers.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a or 2.3, the card's second best: German insurers chased duration as yields fell, while Laura's gap is met once; say covers, never closes: the durations still differ (7.76 against 9.94 years, NUMBERS 1) and the extra Treasuries make the gap harmless if cash waiting earns nothing, never the ten completed by them; rows 21 and 22 merged here.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q195-020: the insurers' weight in German bond buying, quoted second-hand.
Fri 20 Nov: merged into Q195-020: Shin's scales are the same point as an image, and no second image sits beside pencil and ink.
Fri 20 Nov: 3a with row 4, store otherwise: the coupons, worth $93,941 by 2033 (NUMBERS 2), are where she leaves her habitat; the figure is 2.1's already.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.2, one clause on just before: the early side's worst case is priced (waiting at zero after the fee, NUMBERS 2); fix the late side has none to: a bond ending after its payment must be sold at a price no zero-interest test can bound; never that waiting money cannot do worse than zero.
Fri 20 Nov: store: German life policies run 31 years, past the bond market, while her last date, January 2042, lies inside it; the break of row 20.
Fri 20 Nov: a note at most: CANON C12 says it positively, matched payment by payment, never dates, not durations, which reads against TNA l.7; H10-052 holds the same point.
Fri 20 Nov: store: the completion with the 2028 deposit (IPS l.13) is the insurers' falling-yield buying done once and capped; 3.89 points from NUMBERS 1.
Fri 20 Nov: store or Table 3's note: the funds end on or about 15 December by iShares's calendar, 17 days before each payment; payout is net asset value (NUMBERS 3), never fixed.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e or Table 3 row 4, with NUMBERS 8w's $165,000 of $615,000: fix the one place the bond hole leaves no bond, since no T-bond serves the 2033-2036 payments (five rest on funds, four forced, card Q93).

Fri 20 Nov: 3c clause or 3e: the UK habitat was made by a market-value rule, while her ends are counted by payout (IPS l.15; NUMBERS 0), so no price move forces a trade; never cannot move for a stated figure (NUMBERS 3, an early fund end).
Fri 20 Nov: store until Culbertson is read: only the outline was seen.
Fri 20 Nov: store: conceit support only, ink as the habitat's riskless asset; habitat is no dissimilar parallel, and never with a fund's payout as fixed.
